scenario_description: Development continues faster than roads, utilities, schools, housing affordability, and planning capacity can absorb.
interpretation: Stress case: development and population growth outpace infrastructure, housing affordability, road capacity, utilities, and planning capacity.
severity_note: This is the main local stress case because it tests rapid growth against housing, road, utility, and planning capacity.

scenario_description: A geopolitical or macroeconomic shock raises construction materials, fuel, financing costs, logistics costs, and project delay risk.
primary_risk_driver: Materials, fuel, financing, and supply-chain costs
interpretation: Geopolitical cost-shock case: materials, fuel, rates, and logistics costs increase pressure on housing, public infrastructure, and private development.
severity_note: This scenario tests external geoeconomic shock exposure through materials, fuel, financing, and logistics costs.

scenario_description: Development approvals slow during zoning reform or planning review. Infrastructure pressure may ease, but housing supply and developer certainty may weaken.
primary_risk_driver: Rezoning uncertainty and housing supply constraints
interpretation: Policy-friction case: slower approvals may reduce near-term infrastructure pressure but can worsen housing supply constraints and developer uncertainty.
severity_note: This scenario tests policy and planning friction, where lower growth may reduce some infrastructure pressure but increase housing supply risk.

scenario_description: Growth continues, but zoning updates, infrastructure planning, and public investment help the city and county absorb development pressure.
interpretation: Baseline case: local growth remains positive and mostly absorbable if planning, infrastructure, and utility capacity keep pace.
severity_note: This scenario should be interpreted as a controlled baseline rather than a downside shock.
